strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: proposal.apply can recover eligible unapplied create_file items from partial create_file_transaction source evidence under Rust-owned workspace mutation authority.
The recovery path requires WriteWorkspace permission, current approved unconsumed proposals, source fingerprint validation, absent target validation, protected path denial, and symlink rejection.
Apply results record bounded recovery source and per-item evidence without raw file content, raw diffs, command output, environment, secrets, or absolute paths.
A headless caller can resume from partial create transaction evidence and complete remaining absent files without caller-side recovery policy.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances controlled_workspace_tools with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: A headless caller can submit proposal.apply with transaction_recovery_source to complete eligible unapplied items from a partial create_file transaction.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M23.1 can create bounded file transactions and record partial failure evidence, but existing transaction recovery only supports replace_file semantics.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Partial create-file transactions cannot be completed safely by the runtime; callers must abandon or manually recover incomplete generated file sets.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M23.1 implemented original create transaction execution; M22.2 and M22.1 were completion evidence phases unrelated to workspace mutation recovery.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. This extends the existing proposal.apply recovery path using transaction_recovery_source.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. This uses existing apply result and transaction recovery evidence rather than adding a report, digest, history, readiness, preview, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime admits create_file transaction recovery, validates source evidence, revalidates already-created source items, creates only eligible absent targets, and records bounded recovery results.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless automation can decide and perform recovery from durable bounded evidence without holding raw file data or sequencing mutation policy outside Rust.
answers.milestone_progress: This completes the recovery side of M23 controlled file creation apply and should enable M23 closeout after review and merge.

exit_criteria: proposal.apply accepts transaction_recovery_source for eligible create_file transaction recovery without adding a new RPC
The runtime validates same-run latest source evidence, source fingerprint, create_file_transaction operation, failed or partial source status, and unrecovered source state
Already-applied source create items are not rewritten and are revalidated by current SHA-256 against recorded post-write evidence
Recovery items must be current approved unconsumed create_file proposals with expected_target_absent=true and latest absent-target preflight
Successful recovery creates only eligible absent targets with temporary sibling preparation, no-overwrite atomic create, and post-write SHA-256 verification
Failed recovery leaves existing files intact whenever possible, cleans temporary siblings, and does not consume authorization before verified success
Ledger and RPC results remain bounded and do not expose raw file content, raw diffs, prompts, provider responses, stdout/stderr, environment, secrets, or absolute paths
Existing replace-file transaction recovery and create-file transaction apply behavior remain compatible
next_phase_candidate_notes: If M23.2 merges, M23 should move to milestone closeout unless autonomous review identifies a distinct non-wrapper runtime capability gap.
